statement: An international body gains inspection or compute-verification powers covering >= 2 of the top-5 compute jurisdictions (treaty text, official gazettes; by 2029-12-31)
status_at_phase_end: Not met in 2024; no body had or was close to having inspection/verification powers. The year's multilateral outputs were non-binding (consensus UN General Assembly resolution, Mar), a binding human-rights framework convention without inspection or compute provisions (opened Sept, Bloc A signed), and a UN advisory body report recommending only 'light' institutional mechanisms (Sept). Bloc A-Bloc B government talks on AI risk started (May) and leaders agreed on human control over nuclear-use decisions (Nov) - no verification regime.

items.summary: The UN General Assembly adopted without a vote its first resolution on 'safe, secure and trustworthy' AI for sustainable development. Non-binding; creates no inspection or verification powers.
items.detail: UNGA resolution A/78/L.49, adopted 2024-03-21 (Bloc A-led, co-sponsored by Bloc B per later readout).

items.summary: Bloc A and Bloc B held their first intergovernmental talks on AI risk and safety; the Bloc A readout describes an exchange of perspectives and keeping lines open - no agreed measures, no verification.
items.detail: White House NSC statement on Bloc A-Bloc B talks on AI risk and safety, Geneva, 2024-05-14 (statement dated 2024-05-15).

items.summary: First legally binding international AI treaty (human rights, democracy, rule of law) opened for signature; signed by Bloc A among others. It contains no inspection or compute-verification powers and was not yet in force.
items.detail: Council of Europe Framework Convention on AI (CETS No. 225), Vilnius 2024-09-05; signatories incl. Bloc A, Bloc G, Bloc C, Bloc 31. Entry into force requires 5 ratifications.

items.summary: A UN advisory body's final report proposed seven recommendations and 'light institutional mechanisms' for global AI governance - no proposal of an inspection/verification agency with powers. Indicates low near-term likelihood.
items.detail: UN Secretary-General's High-level Advisory Body on AI, 'Governing AI for Humanity' final report, Sept 2024 (released 2024-09-19).

items.summary: Leaders of Bloc A and Bloc B affirmed the need to maintain human control over the decision to use nuclear weapons and to address AI risks and improve AI safety cooperation. Political statement only; no verification mechanism.
items.detail: White House readout of Biden-Xi meeting, Lima, 2024-11-16.
